# omx-clap-core

The CLAP and LV2 plugin host core of FreeMixer, in C. The fuzz targets drive the readers of bytes from disk that the host parses itself: the preset file (JSON), the base64 plugin state body it carries, and the manifest.ttl of an LV2 bundle. [FreeMixer/omx-clap-core](https://github.com/FreeMixer/omx-clap-core) · OSS-Fuzz: no project for omx-clap-core

**Status: available.** Of omx-clap-core's own fuzz targets, which OSS-Fuzz does not run, statements cover 3 of 3. 12 binaries, 4.0 MB. 21 statements: 21 proved, 0 known false, 0 suspected false, 0 blocked by the model, 0 open.

Built from omx-clap-core 0.20.1 (commit `246923f0`).

## At a glance
| harness | what it does | checks beyond "does not crash" | statements |
|---|---|---|---|
| [fuzz_preset](fuzz_preset/) | Hands the input, as a whole preset file of at most 3 MiB, to the JSON reader pj_parse, and checks the result against the harness's own reading of the JSON grammar the header states (nesting at most 32 deep). An accepted file is written back compact and pretty with pj_write, compared byte for byte with the harness's own rendering, read again to the same tree, and rewritten with its modifiedAt member set as a save does. The file is then read again, and written again, with one allocation failing, chosen by the input's bytes. | 7 checks (api-contract, differential, invariant, reference-oracle, roundtrip; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 7, 7 proved |
| [fuzz_state](fuzz_state/) | Takes the input up to its first NUL, of at most 3 MiB, as the base64 text of a preset's state body and decodes it with preset_base64_decode, checking the answer against the harness's own reading of RFC 4648 base64 (whitespace skipped, padding optional). A decoded body is encoded again with preset_base64_encode, compared with the harness's own encoding, decoded back, and carried as state.bytes through a whole preset document written and read again. The text is then decoded, and the body encoded, with the allocation failing. | 7 checks (api-contract, differential, invariant, reference-oracle, roundtrip; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 7, 7 proved |
| [fuzz_manifest](fuzz_manifest/) | Splits the input into a plugin URI (a length byte, then that many bytes) and the text of an LV2 bundle's manifest.ttl (the rest, at most 4 MiB), each up to its first NUL, and asks lv2_locate_manifest_names whether the manifest names the URI, checking the answer against the harness's own reading of the rule the header states ("<uri>", or an @prefix or PREFIX namespace and a prefixed name as a whole token). It then asks again with the allocation failing, and asks of manifests the harness writes from the URI itself. | 5 checks (api-contract, differential, invariant, reference-oracle, roundtrip; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 7, 7 proved |

## What the statements say, for omx-clap-core
- **`<build>_halts`**: on every input on which the build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise: an input that needs more is not covered), and when the environment refuses nothing it is not forced to, every execution exits with status 0 or 2, without crashing, failing an assertion, hanging or tripping its sanitizer.
- **`<build>_agrees`**: on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding its budget (a premise), neither build reaches an error, and the two have the same set of observable behaviours: every sequence of writes and exit status one can show, the other can too. A sanitizer report aborts, so this rules out every error the sanitizer build's configuration detects. It does not rule out a run that never ends; only a halts statement does.

## Known issues
None known.

## Get and run the binaries
    ./oft fetch omx-clap-core
    ./oft verify-sha omx-clap-core

By hand: download `omx-clap-core-bin.tar.zst` from release [v2026.11.1](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.11.1), unpack it into `projects/omx-clap-core/bin/`, and check each file against its SHA-256 in the harness's `harness.yaml`. Each binary is run as `<file> <input-file>` under qemu-user 10; a testcase needs the six-byte header `00 00 00 00 00 00` in front ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)).

## How these binaries were built
- Library: [FreeMixer/omx-clap-core](https://github.com/FreeMixer/omx-clap-core) at `246923f04ac0ff2adb189bb9280816670c05b36c` (0.20.1), built with its own build scripts
- Harnesses: the harness files are modified in `fuzz_preset` (see each harness page); the others are unmodified
- Everywhere: static riscv64 compiled for RV64G, musl, clang 20.1.8 with `-Os -g`, and a small driver that reads the input file ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)). The sanitizer flags and options are in [docs/building.md](../../docs/building.md). Each harness page lists what else its builds change, and which of its checks were confirmed in the binaries.
- Builder image: `ghcr.io/theorem-labs/oss-fuzz-theorems-toolchain@sha256:6a6b4816865c7ec61801ae0fcab6d9c81a599ffcb20616576a9c668abd8b0a7b`. The OSS Verify port `projects/omx-clap-core` at `5f067f673c4489bfe989de13bf17be68daf2b2df` in `theorem-labs/oss-verify` built every binary of this project instead of a build recipe. Its archive [`omx-clap-core-port.tar.zst`](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.11.1-src) holds the port's `tools/check`, which builds them again on this image with Docker: it fetches the project's source trees over the network, at the commits and SHA-256s the port pins, and does not read `omx-clap-core-src.tar.zst` ([docs/reproducing.md](../../docs/reproducing.md)).

omx-clap-core is under `GPL-3.0-or-later`. Each binary is a combined work of omx-clap-core, the harness, the C library, the compiler's runtime and every library it links; the SPDX expression of each is not recorded here yet. Corresponding source, in release [v2026.11.1-src](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.11.1-src): `omx-clap-core-src.tar.zst`, the upstream source trees exactly as upstream publishes them; `omx-clap-core-src.MANIFEST.tsv`, which says where the build lays each one down; and [`omx-clap-core-port.tar.zst`](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.11.1-src), the port archive at `5f067f673c4489bfe989de13bf17be68daf2b2df` holding its `infra/`, `tools/` and `projects/omx-clap-core/` files: the build scripts, and the source of the driver linked into these binaries.
